Subject: Post-demo: deployment route & evidence checklist

Thanks again for your time today — really productive session. Quick recap + asks so we have a single place to track next steps.

Recap (short):
- HealthSprint will process PHI (clinical notes + structured EHR fields) through our inference API to generate triage suggestions.
- Current expected throughput: ~0.5M tokens/day initially, spiking to ~1.5M in Q4.
- Primary concern is auditability and key control; networking (VPC peering) would be preferred if feasible.

Compliance / evidence you asked about:
- SOC 2 Type II report (latest)
- Business Associate Agreement (BAA) and redline path
- Audit logs (access + admin) and retention window (you mentioned 6 months)
- Encryption at rest + TLS in transit + KMS/BYOK options (HSM requirement mentioned by your CISO)
- Network connectivity options (hosted API, Dedicated, or Private VPC/on-prem)

Immediate asks for you (so we can size work):
1) Confirm PHI scope and whether De-identified sets will be used during testing.
2) Confirm preferred deployment route (Private VPC, Dedicated reserved capacity, or Hosted API) and any procurement timelines.
3) Share the vendor-risk questionnaire and the person owning procurement/infosec reviews.

Attachments: Redwood-evidence-checklist.pdf (summary of what we can provide today).

Proposed Redwood next steps:
- I’ll loop in our infra/security leads to confirm gaps and lead times for VPC peering, KMS/HSM integrations, and log-retention changes.
- If you’re leaning Private VPC, we can prepare a short pilot plan (2 weeks on Dedicated or sandbox VPC) to validate latency and integration.

Would you be able to send the completed vendor-risk questionnaire and indicate who should receive the BAA draft?

Thanks,

--

Thanks Soojin — this is helpful. A few clarifications from security/procurement after the call:

- PHI scope: yes, full PHI (patient identifiers + notes + vitals). We’ll provide a small de-identified sample for the initial integration tests.
- Volume: your numbers align with ours (0.5M/day baseline). Q4 spikes are likely dependent on pilot outcomes.
- Preferred deployment: Security wants Private VPC (network isolation + peering) by default. If we can’t get Private done quickly, they’re open to starting on Dedicated capacity while working toward Private.

Security asks (high priority):
1) SOC 2 Type II report and evidence of control operating effectiveness (we’ll need the report and any relevant control summaries).
2) BAA: we need a draft to start legal review. Please send and indicate what clauses are negotiable.
3) KMS: our CISO requests HSM-backed keys (FIPS 140-2/3). Can you support customer-managed keys in an HSM?
4) Logging: retention of audit logs for 6 months (admin + API access + token-level request logs). Can Redwood provide that retention window and an export mechanism to our SIEM?
5) Network: VPC peering or private link — we need documentation on supported network topologies and whether peering requires additional infra on our side.

I attached our vendor-risk questionnaire and initial list of stakeholders (HealthSprint-Vendor-Risk-Questionnaire.xlsx). Legal would like to see a BAA before the intake meeting next week.

If you can provide a short one-pager that maps Redwood features to our asks (SOC2/BAA/KMS/logging/peering) that'll be helpful for our security review.

—Lara

Thanks — quick answers and recommended next steps below. I’ll draft the short one-pager and cost delta for Dedicated vs Private by EOD.

Network / Private VPC:
- Yes — Redwood Private supports customer VPC peering (AWS VPC peering or AWS PrivateLink equivalent). Typical pre-reqs: one allocated CIDR block for peering, firewall rules, and an account-level onboarding call. Lead time: 3–6 weeks for standard setups; 6–10 weeks if cross-account HSM setup or on-prem VPN is required.

KMS / HSM (BYOK):
- We support customer-managed keys via KMS BYOK flows. HSM-backed key material (FIPS 140-2/3) is supported when customers bring keys through our HSM integration or via an HSM-backed KMS provider (AWS CloudHSM / Azure Dedicated HSM). For on-prem or air-gapped, we have an enterprise package but that requires additional ops support and onboarding (4–8 weeks).

Logging & retention:
- We can retain admin + API access + token-level request logs for 6 months via our Optimize/Observability add-on. Exports: we can stream to an S3 bucket or provide periodic S3 exports; we can also push to a customer SIEM via secure transfer. There will be a predictable storage/ingest surcharge — I’ll include a ballpark in the cost delta.

SOC2 / BAA:
- Monica: we have the latest SOC 2 Type II report (2025 cycle) available under NDA; we can share a control summary and the report once NDAs are in place. Our standard BAA draft is attachable and Monica will start the redline-ready draft.

Pilot suggestion:
- Recommend a 2-week Dedicated pilot first (low-friction, rapid provisioning) to validate latency, logging collection to their SIEM, and KMS flows. After pilot success, proceed with Private VPC onboarding to satisfy the security team's isolation requirements. Pilot helps reduce early migration risk and gives procurement something concrete to sign.

Action items / owners:
- Karthik: produce one-pager mapping features to asks + cost delta (Dedicated vs Private) — deliver by EOD.
- Monica: attach SOC2 evidence list and BAA draft; coordinate with Legal.
- Soojin: share vendor questionnaire link with HealthSprint and schedule intake call for next week.

I’ll follow up with the one-pager in ~3–4 hours. If HealthSprint wants to accelerate, we can schedule an infra deep-dive with our networking team.

—Karthik
